results.title: Tag type fetch queue never runs and grows forever
results.reason: The bug is real. Upstream commit ac647fba (Feb 2025) turned an RxList into a ValueNotifier, and since then queue() only does untypedQueue.value.add, which notifies no listener, so getTagTypes has never run in this fork and every booru page adds another UntypedCollection that is never removed. The one-line fix (notify, or call tryGetTagTypes) would switch on a feature that has been dead for the fork's whole life, with new background traffic on every page: one request per tag (concurrency 3, up to 45 per call, re-fed) to a Gelbooru-0.2 site such as rule34.xxx, even for tags from other boorus (fallback to the first booru that populates tags). The answers would also be written into the app-wide tag map and DB. The setting's own text warns 'May cause rate limiting'. That changes behaviour the user relies on and needs a live-site check, so the user should choose: (a) revive fetching and test it on the phone against rule34.xxx, or (b) keep today's behaviour and only stop the queue growing (queue() keeps nothing while nothing reads it).
results.userVisible: internal

results.title: dispose closes the stream before cancelling timers
results.reason: No tick can land during the await (code trace). The only listener, RestartableProgressIndicator, is a descendant, so Flutter unmounts it before HideableAppBar.dispose calls controller.dispose(). close() on a broadcast controller then completes its done future by scheduling a microtask (and with an unpaused listener, the done event is also delivered by microtask). So `await _progressController.close()` resumes after microtasks only, and _cancelTimers runs before the event loop can fire any Timer.periodic tick. No subscription is ever paused, so the scenario cannot happen.

results.title: downloadCustom keeps a paused response stream when the SAF file cannot be created
results.test: test/source_local_server_test.dart: a download whose file cannot be created stops reading instead of pausing on a body it then throws on
results.reason: The bug's description was partly wrong. In Dio 5.11, handleResponseStream's controller does not forward pause or cancel to the socket. So the old code did not hold the connection open: it buffered the rest of the body in memory and threw an uncaught Null-check error from onData. The fix cancels the subscription and throws the same DioException.
